A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Leopard research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or reorganized in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, model and training-data ablations, image-budget experiments, and qualitative examples in the appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds evaluations of Leopard-LLaVA-Pro, additional baselines, and new ablation controls in Tables 4–7.

M1.justification: The allocation equations, image partitioning, pixel shuffling, connectors, and backbone architectures remain unchanged. Leopard-LLaVA-Pro expands pretraining data under the existing architecture; no new encoding component, loss, or inference procedure is specified.

E1.justification: Pro substantially expands pretraining coverage through Recap-COCO-30K, CC-3M, Donut, the Cauldron, and OCR-processed arXiv pages. The original 925K instruction-data inventory remains unchanged. VisualWebBench leaves the formal benchmark list and detailed result tables, although its earlier results remain in Figure 1.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated Llama-3.2-11B and Qwen2-VL-7B comparisons across the multi-image, single-image, and general benchmarks, materially strengthening the comparator set. MM1-7B-Chat's reported comparison rows disappear, although MM1 remains in the model-description table.

E3.justification: v3 introduces an expanded pretraining condition for Pro: Table 2 lists 3.6M pretraining instances versus 0.5M for ordinary Leopard-LLaVA. It also adds no-CoT and 340K-existing-data-only experimental controls. The original models' documented optimizer, batch size, learning rates, epoch count, and image budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 5 and 6 add targeted ablations removing CoT rationales and retaining only existing instruction data. Their three-task multi-image averages are 36.34 and 33.90, versus 40.80 for the full configuration. Earlier encoding, backbone, domain-removal, image-budget, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The added experiments use the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Corresponding Leopard-LLaVA results are revised: Multi-page DocVQA changes from 53.90 to 57.56 and MultiHiertt from 10.76 to 7.70; its five-task average changes from 26.82 to 28.88. v3 adds Pro, new-baseline, and ablation results, while removing some earlier entries. Pro's 37.67 average is a newly reported training condition, not a same-setting improvement. Leopard-Idefics2's retained scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The sub-image allocation equations, scaling rule, partition constraints, and feature-compression mathematics are equivalent. Neither version supplies additional theorems, proofs, or formal guarantees.

C1.justification: The dataset and adaptive encoding remain the two central contributions. v3's abstract adds an explicit efficiency and openness claim based on 1.2M fully open-sourced training instances, contrasted with large in-house datasets; v1 did not make this resource-efficiency claim.

C2.justification: v3 removes v1's qualification that mixed-domain datasets still contain the ablated domains and may explain preserved performance after domain removal. This makes Section 4.5's interpretation less qualified. Most explanations of resolution, image budgets, and backbone effects remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds Pro's pretraining-source and OCR-tool information, changes the repository address, and newly states that data are available alongside code. It omits the earlier explicit 313K ShareGPT4V count and some web-action conversion details. Existing hardware and optimization details are relocated to Appendix A.2, not newly introduced.

R1.justification: Section 3.1.3 and Table 3 extend the existing data-diversity positioning with explicit comparisons against M4-Instruct, Mantis-Instruct, MP-DocStruct1M, and MIMIC-IT. The generic MLLM architecture survey is removed, and pretraining-source references are added. The underlying research gap remains text-rich multi-image understanding.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 is substantially rewritten from a domain-based account into newly collected data, adopted data, and dataset-comparison subsections. Method explanations are condensed, training details move into the appendix, and citation style and publication headers change. This is substantial narrative reorganization beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a single-column journal layout, separates multi-image results from single-image/general results, and splits the original ablation table into component and data tables. It adds the dataset-comparison table and redraws Figure 4's hierarchical composition chart. Most other figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: Stronger baseline comparisons and direct rationale/new-data ablations improve the evidence supporting the central contributions, while the reorganized data description clarifies provenance. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Figure 3 retains older scores despite revised tables, and Pro's 3.6M pretraining total is not reconciled with the stated 4M arXiv pages. The added evidence provides a modest net benefit, without resolving these reliability and reproducibility gaps.
